mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -15.7% to -7.4% over four weeks, indicating a sustained recovery trend. This momentum will continue, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 8.3 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 3 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has risen consistently from 0.6% to 5.9% over four weeks, signaling increased essential-trip frequency. This behavioral shift toward mobility normalcy will spill over into retail-and-recreation visits as confidence in public spaces recovers.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 5.3 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM sustaining above 5.0%, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 3.0% in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains severely depressed at -22.3%, indicating persistent commuting avoidance. This suppression of transit-dependent retail access will constrain RETAIL_REC growth, preventing recovery above -5.0% over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -20.0% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has not improved above -22.3% in the observation window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next four weeks despite TRANSIT remaining below -20.0%, or TRANSIT improves above -15.0%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -10.3% to +2.6% over four weeks, indicating seasonal outdoor-activity normalization. This outdoor-mobility recovery will drive complementary retail-and-recreation visits as weather and holiday seasonality encourage foot traffic.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 0.0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 13.0 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of PARKS sustaining above 0.0%, or PARKS falls below -2.0% in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 16.7% to 14.0% over four weeks, signaling gradual return to out-of-home activity. Combined with rising GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS, this multi-domain mobility rebalancing will drive RETAIL_REC upward as people resume mixed-purpose trips.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 14.5% AND GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 5.0% AND PARKS exceeds 2.0%
evidence_refs: fact:All three series show directional alignment toward out-of-home mobility
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks when all three conditions are met, or any single proxy reverses by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained stable at -15.0% to -16.6% over four weeks, indicating persistent remote-work policy or voluntary avoidance. This sustained workplace suppression will limit retail-and-recreation recovery because commuting-linked retail visits remain unavailable.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains between -16.0% and -15.0% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES variance is only 1.6 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next four weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining stable below -15.0%, or WORKPLACES improves above -10.0%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both severely depressed (-22.3% and -15.0% respectively), creating a compounding suppression of commute-linked retail access. Only if TRANSIT improves by more than 5 percentage points will RETAIL_REC recovery accelerate; otherwise it will plateau below -5.0%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -20.0% AND WORKPLACES remains below -14.0%
evidence_refs: fact:Both series show persistent suppression with minimal week-on-week improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next four weeks when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain suppressed, or either series improves by more than 4 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has crossed above 5.0% and PARKS has turned positive, signaling a regime shift toward normalized essential and discretionary mobility. This dual-signal threshold crossing indicates confidence recovery that will lift RETAIL_REC by at least 2 percentage points within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 5.0% AND PARKS exceeds 0.0% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:Both series achieved threshold conditions in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 1.5 percentage points within two weeks of both thresholds being crossed, or either GROCERY_PHARM or PARKS falls below threshold within one week.
